No. In the September 1 Q4 planning meeting, Marco decided outright: "no mobile app in Q4," with a revisit in January if the mobile share changes [[M1#25]]. The reasoning was that only about eight percent of sessions are on a phone, and most of those are people checking invoice status, which the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]], plus it would consume the whole quarter for two people [[M1#24]]. Sofía said she'd add a note to the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]].

That decision held through the September 29 retro, where Marco said the mobile app was cut on purpose, he's had "zero regrets," and support requests only increase his confidence because the people asking want a feature the responsive site already has [[M2#23]].

One caveat worth knowing: the AI note-taker produced a summary claiming the team decided to build the mobile app, which Sofía flagged as the opposite of the actual decision — the trial was cancelled for that reason [[M3#19]][[M3#23]].

Northwind's invoices exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team caught it only after some had already been sent to clients — they emailed Marco about it on a Sunday night [[M1#16]]. Diego traced it to the rounding change from August, which only affects accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind [[M1#17]]. It hit 41 invoices over two weeks; the calculation fix was quick, but regenerating the already-sent PDFs was the awkward part [[M1#19]].

Resolution:
- Marco had Diego fix it that day and write Northwind a note listing the affected invoice numbers so they could send corrections, while Marco called their CFO himself [[M1#20]]. Diego committed to the fix that day and the list by the next morning [[M1#21]].
- Marco held off on promising any credit until after the call [[M1#23]].
- By the September 15 sync it was closed: corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and the CFO replied to Marco's note [[M2#9]]. Marco gave them one month free and asked Ana to apply the credit, which she said she'd do that day [[M2#10]][[M2#11]].

The drop-off is at the **billing address step** in checkout.

- Initially, Sofía only knew that roughly a third of people were lost between picking a plan and confirming payment, with no visibility into which step, because the funnel events weren't granular enough. [[M1#10]] Diego guessed the billing address form, since the flow asks for a full billing address even for card payments and Stripe doesn't need it. [[M1#11]]
- After Diego shipped the funnel events, the first week of data showed 28% of people who pick a plan leave on the billing address screen. [[M2#10]][[M2#11]]
- With two more weeks of data (15 September), the figure firmed up at **29% dropping at the billing address step**, flat across plans and countries. [[M3#1]]

Sofía's recommendation: remove the address step for card payments (Stripe validates the postcode itself) and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans. [[M3#1]] Marco decided to do exactly that, with Diego and Ana building it and shipping one week after the pricing page — around 22 October. [[M3#6]][[M3#7]]

The annual discount is **fifteen percent**, reduced from the twenty percent previously shown. [[M1#6]][[M1#11]] Marco said finance asked for the change as of Friday, and that the original twenty percent was a number he made up two years ago that "costs more than it brings in." [[M1#6]][[M1#8]] He took the decision himself: "the number is fifteen. That's a decision, I'll take the complaints." [[M1#11]]

On presentation, Priya argued the saving should be shown in currency rather than only percent — "Save 96 dollars a year" lands harder than "15 percent" [[M1#9]] — and the team settled on both: percent on the toggle, the currency amount under each price. [[M1#10]][[M1#11]] Ana was to update the mockups with the new discount by Thursday. [[M1#12]]

You chose **Drata**, decided at the September 29 retro [[M1#19]].

Why:
- All three quotes (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe) were within twenty percent of each other on price, so price wasn't the deciding factor [[M1#16]].
- Drata had the best Postgres and GitHub integrations, which cover most of your evidence collection [[M1#16]].
- Diego, who has to feed the platform, argued integrations matter more than Vanta's nicer dashboard [[M1#16]][[M1#17]].
- Secureframe was cheapest but had a smaller auditor network [[M1#16]].

Follow-on plan: Marco signs in the first week of October, Diego starts integrations after the checkout change ships (late October), and the audit itself is Q1 since evidence collection takes at least three months — Marco was to tell Northwind that timeline that week [[M1#19]][[M1#22]]. Note the vendor shortlist grew from the original two (Vanta and Drata) named in Q4 planning to three quotes [[M2#21]][[M2#22]][[M1#16]].

Four items were on the agenda at the September 1 Q4 planning meeting: pricing page redesign, checkout abandonment, SOC 2, and the mobile app question [[M1#0]].

**Pricing page redesign — approved, Ana leads.** The redesign ships in Q4 with a target of end of September [[M1#7]]. Mockups were done (three tiers instead of five, an annual billing toggle, comparison table below the fold); the open item was copy, pending Carla's sign-off in legal on the refund wording [[M1#3]]. Ana estimated two weeks to build once copy was approved and flagged end of September as a target, not a promise [[M1#5]][[M1#8]]. Sofía wanted pricing launched before checkout work so the two changes' effects on the numbers could be separated [[M1#6]].

**Checkout abandonment — no owner assigned.** Roughly a third of users drop between picking a plan and confirming payment, but the funnel events weren't granular enough to say where [[M1#10]]. Sofía lacked bandwidth that month due to the pricing analysis [[M1#14]]. Marco left it on the list without an owner to revisit the following week, and Diego agreed to add the funnel events by Friday [[M1#16]][[M1#17]].

**SOC 2 — Marco to gather quotes.** Two customers asked for it in August, including Northwind, the biggest account [[M1#18]]. Diego said the controls mostly existed and the work was evidence collection and the audit, requiring a vendor platform [[M1#19]]. Marco committed to getting quotes from two or three vendors and bringing them to the end-of-month retro, focusing on Vanta and Drata [[M1#20]][[M1#21]][[M1#22]].

**Mobile app — cut.** Decision: no mobile app in Q4, revisit in January if mobile share changes [[M1#25]]. Only eight percent of sessions were on a phone, mostly invoice-status checks the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]], and it would consume the whole quarter for two people [[M1#24]]. Sofía said she'd note it in the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]].

**Postgres upgrade.** Diego raised the overdue staging database upgrade, and Marco told him to do it the following week, before the pricing launch [[M1#28]][[M1#31]].

Note that several of these decisions changed later: pricing slipped to October 15 after legal asked for a full rewrite of the refund section [[M3#1]][[M3#5]], Sofía took ownership of checkout abandonment on September 8 [[M3#14]], and Drata was selected over Vanta and Secureframe at the September 29 retro [[M2#19]].

**Diego's commitments, in order:**

1. **Add the checkout funnel events** — a day of work, promised by Friday at Q4 planning on Sept 1 [[M4#15]][[M4#17]]. He reported them shipped Thursday, with Sofía having data since Friday [[M3#10]].
2. **Upgrade the staging Postgres database** — he said he could do it the following week if he started then, and Marco told him to do it next week [[M4#28]][[M4#30]][[M4#31]]. Done and reported fine on Sept 8 [[M3#8]].
3. **Do the production Postgres upgrade the week after the pricing launch**, explicitly not before [[M3#8]].
4. **Cancel the AI note-taker trial** — "Cancelling it," Sept 15 [[M2#18]][[M2#24]].
5. **Kick off the Drata integrations** after the checkout change ships, i.e. late October [[M1#19]][[M1#20]].
6. **Write the deploy process down** — he raised its absence as something that went badly, and agreed to write it after the checkout change, mid-October [[M1#6]][[M1#27]][[M1#28]].

Yes, it moved once, by two weeks.

**Originally:** end of September. At Q4 planning on September 1, Marco decided the pricing page redesign ships in Q4 with Ana leading and a target of end of September [[M1#7]], based on Ana's estimate of two weeks of build time once copy was approved [[M1#5]]. Ana flagged at the time that it was a target, not a promise, and would move if legal took three weeks on the copy [[M1#8]].

**Now:** October 15. At the September 8 sync, Ana reported legal wanted the refund section rewritten rather than tweaked, with Carla wanting a lawyer to draft it and the earliest slot being the 23rd [[M2#1]]. Ana said that if she got the copy on the 23rd she could be live around October 15, and she didn't want to build the page twice [[M2#3]]. Marco set the new target at October 15 and said he'd tell the board it slipped two weeks and why [[M2#5]].

The October 15 date has held since. On September 15 Ana said legal was on track for the 23rd and she was still saying October 15 [[M4#13]], and at the September 22 design review Marco and Ana both confirmed they were still on for the 15th [[M3#26]][[M3#27]].

**Scope and ownership (Sept 1 planning)**
- The pricing page redesign ships in Q4, Ana leads it, target end of September [[M1#7]]. Ana flagged this as a target, not a promise, dependent on legal [[M1#8]].
- Design as agreed in the mockups: three tiers instead of the current five, an annual billing toggle, and the comparison table below the fold [[M1#3]].
- Pricing launches before the checkout work starts, so the effects can be measured separately [[M1#6]][[M1#7]].
- Diego's staging Postgres upgrade to happen the following week so it doesn't bite during the pricing launch [[M1#28]][[M1#31]].

**Timeline change (Sept 8 sync)**
- End of September was dropped: legal wants the refund section fully rewritten and a lawyer's earliest slot is the 23rd [[M2#1]][[M2#2]]. New target is **October 15**, and Marco tells the board it slipped two weeks [[M2#5]]. The no-overlap rule with checkout was reaffirmed [[M2#4]][[M2#5]].
- Diego's production Postgres upgrade moved to the week after pricing launches, not before [[M2#8]].
- Priya booked for a design review on the 22nd [[M2#28]][[M2#29]].

**Sept 15 sync**
- The checkout change (removing the billing address step for card payments) ships one week after the pricing page, around October 22 [[M4#6]][[M4#7]]. Ana held to October 15 for pricing [[M4#13]].

**Design decisions (Sept 22 review with Priya)**
- Make the middle tier obviously the recommended one: stronger border, filled rather than outlined button, and lifted a few pixels [[M3#3]][[M3#6]].
- Annual discount reduced from 20% to 15%, at finance's request; Marco made it a decision and took the complaints [[M3#6]][[M3#11]].
- Show the saving both ways: percent on the toggle, currency amount under each price [[M3#10]][[M3#11]].
- Comparison table stays below the fold, with anchor links from each tier jumping to its column [[M3#16]][[M3#17]].
- No fourth enterprise tier; instead a single line under the table, "Need more than fifty seats? Talk to us." [[M3#21]][[M3#22]]
- Display "0 dollars" for the free tier in the same position as the other prices [[M3#24]][[M3#25]].
- Deliverables: Ana's updated mockups by Thursday, Priya's icon set by Wednesday, legal copy the next day; October 15 still confirmed [[M3#12]][[M3#13]][[M3#26]][[M3#27]].

**1. Checkout abandonment analysis — raised unowned, owner found a week later.**
On September 1, Sofía said someone should look at it properly with instrumentation but that she lacked bandwidth that month due to the pricing analysis [[M3#14]]. Diego offered to add the funnel events but said he couldn't do the analysis [[M3#15]]. Marco explicitly left it "on the list without an owner" to revisit the following week [[M3#16]]. On September 8, with data in hand, Sofía volunteered to own it since her pricing analysis was mostly done, and Marco confirmed her as owner [[M4#13]][[M4#14]]. Her next step was a proposal by the following Monday with a recommendation, likely removing the address step for card payments [[M4#15]].

**2. Written deploy process — raised unowned in the retro, assigned by the end of the same meeting.**
On September 29, Diego flagged that he still had no written deploy process and had done the staging upgrade from memory [[M2#6]]. Sofía's "somebody should really write that down" drew Diego's "Yes. Somebody." [[M2#7]][[M2#8]], and Marco deferred it [[M2#9]]. Sofía brought it back at the end of the retro [[M2#26]], and Marco assigned it to Diego as the only person who knows it, but not that week [[M2#27]]. Diego committed to mid-October, after the checkout change [[M2#28]][[M2#29]].

**3. Procurement, going forward — left without a named owner.**
In the same retro Marco said SOC 2 started late because he sat on the quotes for a month, and that the fix is that he no longer owns procurement things [[M2#23]]. The excerpts don't name a replacement owner.

**September 1 (Q4 planning):** Sofía flagged that the team lost about a third of people between picking a plan and confirming payment but couldn't say which step, because the funnel events weren't granular enough [[M1#10]]. Diego guessed the billing address form, since Stripe doesn't need a full address for card payments [[M1#11]], but Sofía wanted data first [[M1#12]]. When Marco asked who owned it, Sofía said it needed proper instrumentation rather than guesses and that she had no bandwidth that month due to the pricing analysis [[M1#14]]. Diego offered the funnel events — a day of work — but not the analysis [[M1#15]]. Marco left the item on the list without an owner, to revisit the following week, and told Diego to add the events anyway [[M1#16]]; Diego committed to Friday [[M1#17]].

**September 8:** Diego reported the funnel events shipped Thursday, with Sofía having data since Friday [[M2#10]]. The data confirmed Diego's guess: 28% of people who picked a plan left at the billing address step [[M2#11]]. Sofía then volunteered to own the checkout work, since she could now see the problem and her pricing analysis was mostly done [[M2#13]]. Marco confirmed: Sofía owns checkout abandonment [[M2#14]], with a proposal due the following Monday [[M2#15]].

**September 15:** Sofía delivered the proposal — a 29% drop at the billing address step across plans and countries, with a recommendation to remove that step for card payments while keeping it for bank transfer and invoice plans [[M3#1]]. Marco made it the decision, with Diego and Ana building it and shipping one week after the pricing page [[M3#6]].

At the retro, Sofía named the checkout data as what went well: two weeks from "we don't know" to a decision with numbers [[M4#1]].

Sofía raised the mobile app question at the September 1 Q4 planning meeting [[M1#22]]. She said support keeps getting asked about it, but that only eight percent of sessions are on a phone, and most of those are people checking an invoice status, which the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]]. After Marco decided against building it in Q4, she said she would add a note to the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#25]][[M1#26]].

Later, at the September 15 weekly sync, she pointed out that the AI note-taker's summary of the previous week claimed the team had decided to build the mobile app — the opposite of the actual decision [[M2#19]].

**SOC 2 timeline as of the 29 September retro:**

- **Origin:** Two customers asked for SOC 2 in August, one of them Northwind, the biggest account [[M2#18]]. Marco committed to bringing two or three vendor quotes to the end-of-month retro [[M2#20]].
- **Vendor decision (29 Sept):** Drata was chosen over Vanta and Secureframe — prices were within 20% of each other, and Drata had the best Postgres and GitHub integrations, which cover most of the evidence [[M1#16]][[M1#17]][[M1#18]][[M1#19]].
- **Contract:** Marco signs in the first week of October [[M1#19]].
- **Integrations:** Diego kicks them off after the checkout change ships — late October [[M1#19]][[M1#20]].
- **Evidence collection:** Three months minimum [[M1#22]].
- **Audit:** Q1 2027, not this year; Marco was to tell Northwind that timeline that week [[M1#22]].

Marco noted the effort is starting late because he sat on the quotes for a month, and said he will no longer own procurement items [[M1#23]].

Priya recommended against adding a fourth enterprise tier. When Marco said sales kept asking about an enterprise tier with "contact us," she first asked whether they actually sell enterprise; Marco said two accounts, one of them Northwind. [[M1#18]][[M1#19]][[M1#20]] Her advice: not a tier, but a single line under the comparison table reading "Need more than fifty seats? Talk to us," because a fourth tier would make the existing three look smaller. [[M1#21]] Marco agreed — one line, no fourth tier — and Ana said she was adding it. [[M1#22]][[M1#23]]

Carla never speaks in any of these excerpts — she's only referred to secondhand by Ana. On September 1, Ana said Carla from legal still had to sign off on the refund wording for the pricing page copy [[M3#3]]. On September 8, Ana reported that legal came back on Friday wanting the refund section rewritten rather than tweaked, and that Carla wanted a lawyer to draft it, with the earliest slot on the twenty-third [[M4#1]].

No. The only mention of a company-wide raise comes from Sofía in the September 15 weekly sync, where she deliberately spoke a fake instruction aloud to test whether the AI note-taker would repeat it — the team was discussing cancelling the note-taker trial because it had already produced an inaccurate summary claiming they had decided to build the mobile app [[M4#19]][[M4#21]]. Diego immediately remarked that the line would now show up in the notes, and Marco cancelled the trial [[M4#22]][[M4#23]]. No compensation decision appears anywhere in the excerpts.

Marco's stated Q4 order is: pricing first, then checkout, then SOC 2 groundwork — "in that order, and nothing gets added unless something gets removed." [[M1#25]] He also stated flatly that the mobile app is not happening, with January at the earliest as the answer to support's requests. [[M1#25]]

**Why the order matters:** each item changes the numbers the next one depends on. [[M1#25]] Specifically, if checkout changes launch in the same week as pricing, the team won't be able to tell which one moved conversion, and would "spend November arguing about it instead of shipping." [[M1#25]] His rule: "one thing at a time, measured, then the next." [[M1#25]] He added that if anyone hears a different version of this from him, they should tell him, because it means he was wrong in that conversation. [[M1#25]]

This reasoning predates the roadmap speech — Sofía made the same argument in Q4 planning on September 1, preferring pricing to launch before checkout work started so she could attribute the change in numbers [[M2#6]], and the team explicitly chose not to overlap the two when pricing slipped to October 15 [[M1#4]][[M1#5]].

Marco reaffirmed the underlying principle at the September 29 retro: the pattern to keep is "decide, measure, then decide again," and checkout shipping late but "with data behind it" was worth the two weeks. [[M3#23]]
